model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis, logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴) and classification accuracy (ACC, y-axis, linear scale from 35% to 65%) for six different methods: Base (black circles, solid line), FT (blue downward triangles, solid line), IKE (red upward triangles, solid line), MEND (brown diamonds, solid line), MEMIT (purple pentagons, solid line), and ROME (green squares, solid line). As the co-occurrence number increases, all methods generally show an upward trend in accuracy. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence levels, starting at ~51% and rising to ~66%. MEND and MEMIT follow similar trajectories, beginning near 44% and 43% respectively and increasing to ~56% and ~55%. IKE and FT show more moderate gains, starting at ~43% and ~40% and reaching ~49% and ~48%. The Base method remains the lowest, starting at ~38% and plateauing around 44%.
